clue.text: Successor to Randall, almost courteous: an internationalist type

parts.note: Cosmo Lang succeeded Randall Davidson as Archbishop of Canterbury

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: courteous means polite

explanation.surface: Someone describes the man who followed Randall as nearly polite and thoroughly worldly.
explanation.walkthrough: Randall Davidson was Archbishop of Canterbury; Cosmo Lang came after him. 'almost' cuts the last letter from POLITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A worldly person at home in many countries is a citizen of the world, an internationalist type.

clue.text: Beast of burden returning to a legendary settlement

parts.note: a camel carries loads across deserts

indicators.note: returning signals that the little word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: A pack animal heads back to a fabled town.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthurian legend places King Arthur's court in a fabled castle and town of this name.

clue.text: A little learning with zero activity or movement

parts.note: SCH is a short form of school or scholar, a little piece of learning

indicators.note: activity suggests the letters are set busily moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that a smattering of education leads to doing nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes 'a little learning is a dangerous thing'; 'activity' shuffles SCH and ZERO.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a lively section of a symphony or sonata is called a movement, and this is one such piece.

clue.text: She needs no provocation to get involved in a row

definitions.text: She needs no provocation to get involved in a row

parts.words: She needs no provocation to get involved in a row
parts.note: a row here is the act of rowing a boat, not a quarrel, so the woman joins a crew willingly

explanation.surface: A woman always ready for an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A female rower takes part in a row on the water without any quarrel being needed.

clue.text: Where shooting is likely to start

definitions.meaning: a film is shot on a set

explanation.definitionFit: Filming takes place on set, and the run-together word means a beginning or outbreak.

clue.text: Former general taking heart from fruit and flower arrangement …

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of General Dwight Eisenhower

indicators.note: taking heart from means the central letters are removed

parts.note: a banana is a fruit

explanation.surface: An old soldier pulls the middle out of a piece of fruit while arranging flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking heart from' removes NA, the central pair of BANANA, leaving BANA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese art of arranging flowers is known by this name.

clue.text: … stirring a subordinate to get fruit order cancelled

parts.note: a GI is an American private soldier, low in rank

indicators.note: cancelled means the named letters are struck out of the word

parts.note: a potato is the produce of a plant, loosely a fruit of the earth
PO is a postal order

explanation.surface: Agitating a junior soldier to have an order for fruit withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cancelled' strikes PO (postal order) out of POTATO, leaving TATO.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical direction means played in an agitated, restless manner, so stirring.

clue.text: Where we make a show of disrespect to the French?

definitions.text: Where we make a show of disrespect to the French?

parts.words: Where we make a show of disrespect to the French?
parts.note: the island nation across the Channel from France, long a traditional rival, described by Shakespeare's phrase for it

explanation.surface: Asking where people show rudeness towards the French.
explanation.walkthrough: John of Gaunt in Shakespeare's Richard II calls England 'this sceptred isle'; the English and French traditionally trade jibes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's poetic phrase for England, where the English traditionally mock their French neighbours.

clue.text: Essential oil adding nothing to speed in vehicle

indicators.note: in means the speed and nothing are put inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
MPH, miles per hour, measures speed
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Something about an essential oil being added to a fast-moving vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic substance is distilled from the camphor tree and used as an essential oil.

clue.text: Officer of the crown, if seen in fresh rig

indicators.note: seen in places the word if inside the other letters
rig means to arrange or fix, so the letters of fresh are rearranged

explanation.surface: An official of the Crown spotted wearing a new outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rig' looks like the noun for an outfit but is the anagram signal; 'seen in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheriff is a county official appointed on behalf of the Crown.

clue.text: One with whom the social services take issue

definitions.text: One with whom the social services take issue

parts.words: One with whom the social services take issue
parts.note: issue means offspring: social services place children with a carer, not argue with her

explanation.surface: Someone the welfare department is quarrelling with.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who takes in children placed by social services looks after their issue, meaning offspring.

clue.text: Actress needing a friend to trust

parts.note: a pal is a friend
trow is an old word meaning to believe or trust

explanation.surface: A performer who needs a companion she can rely on.
explanation.definitionFit: Gwyneth Paltrow is an American film actress, so the surname stands for one actress.

clue.text: A Bill Gates' badly downloaded programme and they could get into hot water

definitions.text: they could get into hot water

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for bill, as in B/E for bill of exchange

explanation.surface: A poorly downloaded Microsoft program, and things that could end up in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' shuffles A, B and GATES. 'Get into hot water' is the misleading idiom for trouble; the bags go literally into hot water.
explanation.definitionFit: Small bags of leaves are steeped in hot water to brew a cup of tea.

clue.text: Contents of treasure-trove belonging to a bygone age

indicators.note: contents of means the letters are found inside the words treasure-trove

explanation.surface: A hoard of ancient treasure contains items from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro styles imitate or come from an earlier era, so they belong to a bygone age.

clue.text: Yard held individual with a drug

parts.note: Scotland Yard is the Met, London's Metropolitan Police
held means had, as in possessed
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: The police hold someone with narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police, the Met.
explanation.definitionFit: Methadone is a synthetic opioid drug used to treat heroin addiction.

clue.text: They work in Spanish and Latin production

indicators.note: production means the letters are put together in a new form

parts.note: et is the Latin word for and

explanation.surface: People who perform in a show staged in Spanish and Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' shuffles SPANISH with ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors work on the stage, and thespian is a word for an actor.

clue.text: Spooner's activity of many prior to marriage

indicators.note: Spooner's signals a swap of the opening sounds of two words, after Rev. Spooner

parts.note: all, an activity for everyone
a dance is an activity

explanation.surface: Spooner describes a pastime shared by many people before the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: An all-dance is everyone dancing; Spooner swaps its opening sounds to give 'dall-ance', the flirting that may come before a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliance is light flirtation or courtship, the toying that precedes marriage.

clue.text: Household god can turn up at a Mediterranean resort

parts.note: a lar is a Roman household god

indicators.note: turn up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A domestic deity may turn up at a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses CAN to NAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Larnaca is a coastal resort town in Cyprus, on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Like Caesar without a hazard

indicators.note: without means the letter a is left out

parts.note: imperial, like an emperor such as Caesar

explanation.surface: Being like Caesar with no danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes A out of IMPERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To hazard something is to put it at risk, which is to endanger it.

clue.text: Downbeat mood of Gateshead weaver?

parts.note: read as Gates head, the head or first letter of Gates
a loom is a weaving machine

explanation.surface: A gloomy weaver from Gateshead, the town in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town on the Tyne in north-east England; split it as 'Gates head' to get G. A loom does the weaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloom is a state of low spirits, a downbeat mood.

clue.text: Mother's ruin's part of 7, which is said to be curative

definitions.text: which is said to be curative

parts.note: mother's ruin is a slang name for gin, plus the possessive S
7-down is England, of which ENG is an abbreviated part

explanation.surface: Gin is part of England, and supposedly cures you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother's ruin' is old British slang for gin. 7-down is SCEPTRED ISLE, England, giving ENG.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginseng is a root traditionally reputed to have healing, restorative powers.

clue.text: His son ain't about to be conceived

definitions.text: His son ain't about to be conceived

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: His son is not going to be conceived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SON AIN'T. The whole clue is the definition: such a man's habits mean no child is conceived.
explanation.definitionFit: A man practising self-gratification or withdrawal produces no offspring, so no son is conceived.

clue.text: Fight that's feared by shepherds

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A brawl that worries sheep farmers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'something feared by shepherds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapie is a fatal disease of sheep, a dread of every flock keeper.

clue.text: All's said to be wrong with the Spanish

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: Everything is supposedly mistaken with the Spanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All's said' means a word that sounds like 'all', namely awl; an elsin is a Scots word for an awl.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsin is a Scottish dialect word for a shoemaker's awl, a homophone of all.

clue.text: Desperate character in Pentonville cut short by hanging

indicators.note: in places the comic character inside the shortened prison name
cut short means the end of the word is chopped off

parts.note: Desperate Dan is a character in the Dandy comic

explanation.surface: A desperate inmate of Pentonville prison has his life ended by the noose.
explanation.walkthrough: Pentonville is a London prison. 'cut short' trims it to PENT, and 'in' puts DAN, from the British comic strip Desperate Dan, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendant is an ornament that hangs, and pendant as an adjective means hanging.

clue.text: Heath's relative sorted 21

indicators.note: sorted means the letters are arranged into a new order

parts.note: 21-across, the sheep disease

explanation.surface: A relative of Edward Heath sorted out an earlier clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Edward Heath, the British prime minister; the heath is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Epacris is a genus of Australian heath-like shrubs, a relative of the heaths.

clue.text: Dutch given to drink — that's fishy

indicators.note: given to means the wife is added after the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink
my old Dutch is Cockney slang for one's wife

explanation.surface: A Dutchman is fond of drink, which is suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Dutch' (from duchess) is Cockney slang for a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The alewife is a North American fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Visual challenge of Spooner's naval battle

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: sailing, to do with ships
a fight is a battle

explanation.surface: Spooner describes a sea battle as an eyesight problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Deteriorating eyesight is a challenge to one's vision.
